Plastic.disposal_instructions: Clean the item if possible and place it in the appropriate plastic recycling bin. Follow local recycling rules.
Plastic.summary: Recyclable plastic polymer containers, bottles, and packaging.
segregation_steps: Clean the item if possible and place it in the appropriate plastic recycling bin.
Follow local recycling rules.
Empty leftover liquids and rinse out greasy residues.
Crush plastic bottles to save space in the recycling bin.
Plastic.examples: Water bottles, beverage containers, milk jugs, detergent containers, plastic tubs.
Plastic.environmental_fact: Recycling plastic prevents persistent microplastic contamination in oceans and soil.

Paper.disposal_instructions: Keep it clean and dry, then place it in the paper recycling bin. Avoid recycling heavily contaminated paper.
Paper.summary: Dry cellulose paper, cardboard boxes, and paper packaging.
segregation_steps: Keep it clean and dry, then place it in the paper recycling bin.
Avoid recycling heavily contaminated paper.
Flatten cardboard boxes and packaging cartons.
Remove sticky plastic tape, bubble wraps, and metal clips if possible.
Paper.examples: Cardboard boxes, notebooks, newspapers, office copy paper, magazines, clean envelopes.
Paper.environmental_fact: Recycling paper conserves trees, fresh water, and electrical energy.

Metal.disposal_instructions: Separate metal items and place recyclable metal in the appropriate recycling bin.
Metal.summary: Aluminum, steel, and tin metal containers.
segregation_steps: Separate metal items and place recyclable metal in the appropriate recycling bin.
Empty all contents and rinse out food or drink residues.
Push metal lid flaps inside cans to prevent sharp edges.
Do not mix electronic waste or batteries in regular metal recycling bins.
Metal.examples: Soda and beverage cans, tin food cans, aluminum foil trays, metal jar lids.
Metal.environmental_fact: Metal can be recycled repeatedly without degradation in structural quality.

Glass.disposal_instructions: Handle carefully and place recyclable glass in the designated glass collection bin. Do not put broken glass into a normal recycling bin unless local rules allow it.
segregation_steps: Handle carefully and place recyclable glass in the designated glass collection bin.
Do not put broken glass into a normal recycling bin unless local rules allow it.
Rinse glass bottles and jars clean of food or drink residues.
Separate non-glass caps, lids, and corks.
Glass.examples: Beverage bottles, glass jam jars, culinary condiment jars, medicine vials.
Glass.environmental_fact: Glass is 100% recyclable infinitely with zero loss in purity.

Organic.disposal_instructions: Put suitable food scraps and garden waste in a compost bin or an approved organic-waste collection bin.
Organic.summary: Biodegradable organic matter suitable for composting.
segregation_steps: Put suitable food scraps and garden waste in a compost bin or an approved organic-waste collection bin.
Keep plastic wrappers, stickers, and non-biodegradable packaging out of organic waste.
Drain excess liquid before disposal to prevent odors and bin leakage.
Use home compost pits or municipal green bin collection.
Organic.examples: Fruit peels, vegetable skins, food scraps, tea leaves, coffee grounds, garden clippings.
Organic.environmental_fact: Composting organic matter produces rich organic soil fertilizer and reduces landfill emissions.
